flawed_step: Step 3: inferring that the induced graph on the six neighbours of a vertex must be two disjoint triangles. Steps 1–2 only show that this induced graph is 2-regular; it may instead be a 6-cycle.
assessment_summary: For any vertex v, each neighbour has exactly lambda=2 neighbours within N(v), so G[N(v)] is 2-regular on six vertices. The attempted uniqueness proof stops because this allows both 2K3 (as in the rook graph) and C6. The alternative is genuinely realized by the Cayley graph on Z_4^2 with connection set {±(1,0), ±(0,1), ±(1,1)}: direct difference counting gives parameters (16,6,2,2), while every neighbourhood induces C6. Hence it is not isomorphic to the rook graph, whose neighbourhoods induce 2K3.
